title: Road safety plan and Erbsville North planning approved
subtitle: Land donation, brownfield grant renewal, capital funding release, digital services update, and a new Staff Association agreement.
overview: Council approved a road safety and traffic calming plan and updated the Traffic and Parking By-law {{vote:m7}}. Staff described a data-driven approach that ranks locations by collisions and speed, and plans to bundle measures at each location. Council also approved terms of reference for a Master Environmental Servicing Plan and District Plan for the Erbsville North area {{vote:m8}}, which will guide future development there.

Council accepted a donation of 3.69 acres of environmentally sensitive woodland on Wilmot Line {{vote:m9}}. It released capital funding for building renewal and the Uptown Rink {{vote:m10}}, and removed the expiry date on the City-wide Brownfield Tax Increment Grant program {{vote:m11}}. Council also approved the 2025-2028 Staff Association agreement {{vote:m12}}.

Council received a digital services update {{vote:m6}}. During questions, staff agreed to look at a veterans banner program and a veterans crosswalk for 2025 and to reinstate the Lee Avenue centre line, by spring if needed. Councillors also asked staff to consider compiling a list of suspected brownfield sites.

decisions.detail: Council received the road safety and traffic calming report and approved amendments to Traffic and Parking By-law #08-077.
Council approved terms of reference for a Master Environmental Servicing Plan and District Plan for the Erbsville North area.
Council accepted a donation of 3.69 acres of environmentally sensitive woodland at 0 Wilmot Line and authorized signing the purchase and sale agreement.
Council released funding for the Building Capital Renewal project for 2024, 2025 and 2026, and 2024 funding for the Uptown Rink Renewal, from the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund.
Council removed the expiry date on the City-wide Brownfield Tax Increment Grant program so it continues until Council dissolves the project area, and directed staff to notify the Region.
Council approved the terms of settlement with the Staff Association covering January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2028.
Council approved renewing the lease with the Region of Waterloo and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it.

debate: On road safety, councillors asked how locations with several collision types would be treated. Staff said measures would be installed together at each location to limit disruption. Several councillors asked for fuller data, including collisions on regional roads and near misses that police do not record. Staff said a new grant will add connected-vehicle data on near misses and hard braking.

One councillor questioned whether the proposed measures at a top-ranked pedestrian collision intersection were too minor. Staff replied that they target the root problem of poor sight lines through lane alignment, parking changes and daylighting.

On Erbsville North, councillors stressed that the watershed study should be scoped widely enough to be done once, given past studies that had to be redone. The consultant said the study area overlaps known drainage areas and would be expanded if needed. Councillors also pressed for a granular District Plan and for flood risk and wetland benefits to be considered.

Some councillors were disappointed that Indigenous engagement was still at an early stage and questioned whether the City should lead it rather than the landowners. The consultant said initial outreach had begun through the archaeological assessment and that it would follow City protocols. One councillor also raised a resident suggestion to close Conservation Drive to vehicles at Snow Crest.

On brownfields, councillors asked for a list of known or suspected sites. Staff said there is no inventory and that confirming contamination would be costly, but that a list of likely sites based on past uses could be prepared. Councillors supported a review of the program's incentives.
